D()'. 2.13.18 (coursier) reports the exhaustivity warning in both orders. on_base and on_2_13_18 are as the finding says; Scala 3.7.4 was run by the hunter, not re-run.
user_impact: Any mixed Scala/Java module on 2.13.19 that matches on a sealed Java interface or class written without a permits clause, when no class declared through `class` or `interface` in that Java file carries final, abstract, private or protected. That covers the usual Java 17 algebraic data type (sealed interface with record cases), enum cases and `non-sealed class` cases, nested or top-level. Every such match loses its exhaustivity warning and a match with two or more type cases gets a false 'unreachable code', which fails a -Werror build. Macros that read knownDirectSubclasses of such a type get the empty set.
fixability: clear cut: in JavaParsers.classDecl and interfaceDecl write `mods.hasFlag(Flags.SEALED)`; the bare SEALED there is the token constant JavaTokens.SEALED = 45 inherited from CommonTokens, not the flag. Only warnings change. Add a test whose implementors are all records, since the existing tests pass through their `final class` cases.
regression: in unreleased 2.13.19: scala/scala PR 11329 (lrytz, 'Fix cyclic references when completing sealed Java classes', commit ed1bec6de3, merged 2026-11-03). It exposed a parser mistake present since 2.13.11 (scala/scala PR 10348, commit a0f546d8c9).
links: None of the earlier waves or wave four has it; PM1 (retronym/scala PR 622) is a different cause of a wrong unreachable-code warning. No scala/bug ticket found (queries: sealed java record exhaustive joint; java sealed permits unreachable code; sealed Java record exhaustivity).
note: The cause is in the Java parser, made visible by the namer change; the pattern matcher's analysis is correct for the children it is given. The hunter's explanation (records and enums are not collected) is wrong. JavaParsers.scala:986 and :1048 test `mods.hasFlag(SEALED)` where SEALED resolves to the token number 45 = bits 0, 2, 3, 5 = PROTECTED | PRIVATE | ABSTRACT | FINAL. So the per-unit set patmat.javaClassesByUnit is created only when some class or interface in the file has one of those modifiers, and never because of `sealed` itself (single-stepping interfaceDecl for `public sealed interface S` skips the assignment). Until PR 11329 that set only chose which classes to force, and children were registered when each subclass was completed, so the mistake was harmless. PR 11329 computes the children of a sealed Java class without a permits clause from that set (Namers.enterJavaClass, unitClasses), so a missing set now means no children. Confirmed by variants on w3-base: three records fail; one record plus two final classes works; top-level records fail and start working when an unrelated `final class Z {}` is added to the file; three `non-sealed class` cases fail; three enums fail; an explicit permits clause works. The fix was not built (no sbt in this review).
